configuration_yard.name: Configuration Yard
configuration_yard.description: Three artifacts in this corpus carry an axis called `configuration` and all three mean the same question - where the mass is at t = 0, the one thing gravity cannot derive for you - while naming three different KINDS of answer. example_3_2's ring, column and shells are ARRANGEMENTS, the way a stage manager arranges. nbody_simulation's cloud, disc, shells and lattice are STATISTICAL SHAPES, said as a distribution. three_body_problem's figure_eight and lagrange are EXACT SOLUTIONS - named, published, measure-zero families in a chaotic problem, which you cannot reach by drawing a shape. This yard puts seven of those words in one 1.00 x 1.00 x 1.00 cage, three bodies each, equal masses, and integrates the real gravitational ODE for a fixed 1.360 s at a fixed 0.0005 s step. The point is what the three kinds look like: at `start` they are the same kind of picture, and `ring` and `lagrange` are LITERALLY the same picture, three bodies at three identical points. At `path` they part. At `drift` - the same run again with body 0 moved half a millimetre - the arrangements come apart by more than the system's own radius while the exact solutions and the hierarchical class hold to within a hundredth of it. Nothing animates, nothing is random, nothing is printed.
dev_themes: one word, three kinds of answer
interactions: stand at reading=start and walk the configuration axis: seven placements, and two of them - ring and lagrange - are the same three points, because an arrangement and a theorem look identical until something moves

put configuration=ring beside configuration=lagrange at reading=path: the same three points, one turning rigidly forever and one breathing down to a third of its size, and the only difference in the file is a factor of 0.70 on the speed

put configuration=figure_eight at reading=path and count the curves: there is ONE, because in a choreography all three bodies run the same track - the three tubes are nested only so you can see that all three are there
walk the reading axis at configuration=column and at configuration=lagrange side by side: the same half-millimetre nudge is invisible in one and throws the other out of the yard

stand at reading=drift and look for colour: gold alone means the perturbed run is still inside the unperturbed one; wherever a body colour appears beside the gold, the two futures have parted by more than a tube width
configuration_yard.capacity: SEE that `configuration` names three different kinds of thing - a distribution you can sketch, an arrangement you can place, and a solution you must derive - and that a photograph of the starting positions cannot tell them apart, because the difference is not in where the bodies are but in what happens next

spatial_needs.footprint_note: Every single-layout variant is the SAME body, because the body is the YARD: a round plate of radius 0.50 m, a rim ring, four 0.030 m posts 1.00 m tall at radius 0.46 and a top ring, all axis-aligned and drawn before either axis is consulted. The figure inside is held under the plate's radius by construction - the widest start is hierarchical's third body at 0.360 m, the widest UNPERTURBED track is lattice at 0.4249 m, and drawing stops at CLIP_R = 0.44 m, which plus the widest tube (0.0120) is 0.4520 - so the world box is 1.00 x 1.00 x 1.00 in all twenty-one cells and one grid cell holds it. layout=ladder stands all seven configurations in a row at 1.15 m pitch (about 7.9 m wide) and is a design view, not a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants and the same integrator; no Godot was run. The box is the YARD and nothing else: the plate spans +-0.50 in x and z, the posts run y 0 to 1.00, and the drawn figure's own extent runs from 0.555 m across at shells to 0.904 m at a clipped drift track - which is exactly why the yard exists and why the AABB is identical in all twenty-one variants by construction.

dna.default: configuration=ring, reading=start. ring is the default because it is the ARRANGEMENT half of the registered null and because it is example_3_2's own shipped value - the legacy lineage of the oldest of the three members' axes. start is the default because it is the reading in which the thesis is a null: at start the sheet's FIRST and SEVENTH tiles, ring and lagrange, are the same picture to the byte, and everything this bench argues is about what that identity conceals. The two ends of the configuration axis being the identical frame is deliberate - it is the pair a reader is least likely to compare by eye. NOTE WHAT THIS COSTS: the default is the LEAST inked cell in the sheet - three spheres in a cage, no tracks - which would normally be a bad tile to solve framing on. It is not, because framing here is set by the yard and the yard is identical in every variant, so the camera distance is the same whichever cell is measured. Subject share at the default is 20.95% of frame, against 23.64% at the busiest (lattice/drift), so no tile is anywhere near the blank bar.
dna.note: WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, and where each word came from. THE FAMILY FIRST, and it is a family by WORD rather than by subject: three artifacts declare an axis literally named `configuration`, and each states that it turns the initial condition. example_3_2_forces_with_arbitrary_angular_motion_vr (ring | column | shells | fan | scatter) says in its own header that the word is 'where the mass and the attitude are before the law touches either', and its values are ARRANGEMENTS - its ring is a circle with a jittered radius and a flat tangential 0.3 at every radius, a speed nothing derived. nbody_simulation (cloud | disc | shells | binary | lattice) says the word turns 'the one thing gravity cannot derive for you: where the mass IS at t = 0', and four of its five values are RNG draws - its words name a distribution, not a placement, and it says so itself: 'figure_eight and lagrange are theorems about exactly three bodies and mean nothing at twenty'. three_body_problem (pinwheel | figure_eight | lagrange | hierarchical | near_collision) holds the third kind: two of its five are EXACT SOLUTIONS with published constants in its CONFIGURATIONS table. So one word, three kinds of answer, and nobody in the family has stood them next to each other. THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: a photograph of the starting positions cannot tell an arrangement from a theorem, because the difference between them is not in the picture at all - it is in the velocity field, which no still can show, and in the stability, which only a perturbation can. The disagreement available, and it is fair: this is a claim about what a STILL can carry, and someone could reasonably answer that nobody was ever confused about this and that the three vocabularies were never meant to be one axis - in which case `configuration` is three homonyms and the family should say so. CONFIGURATION, seven values, each a member's word. ring = example_3_2's, three bodies on a circle of radius SYS_R = 0.30 in the XZ plane at angles 90, 210 and 330 degrees, with equal tangential speeds at RING_FRAC = 0.70 of what the theorem requires - the stage manager's guess, and the 0.70 is THIS BENCH'S number, declared rather than inherited. What it turns out to be is the pass's best surprise: the equilateral triangle is a CENTRAL CONFIGURATION, so any purely tangential equal speed gives a homographic solution - the triangle stays exactly equilateral and breathes, at 0.70 down to r = 0.09735 (eccentricity 0.51) and back, 1.86 times in the window, verified as a minimum pairwise separation of 0.1686 = 0.09735 * sqrt(3). The arrangement is not wrong about the shape. It is wrong about everything else, and `drift` is where that is cashed. column = example_3_2's, the three stacked on the vertical axis at COL_SPAN = 0.30 spacing, each given the same by-eye speed in a horizontal direction 120 degrees from its neighbours' - which is example_3_2's own statement, whose velocity is indexed by i/n*TAU while its position is not. shells = THE CONTESTED WORD, and the two members DO NOT MEAN THE SAME THING BY IT. nbody's shells is two concentric SPHERES sampled at random (sin(v)cos(u), cos(v), sin(v)sin(u) at 0.45 and 1.0 of spawn_radius, alternating by i%2, at rest) - a sampling statement that has nothing to say below N of about twenty. example_3_2's shells is two horizontal RINGS at two heights (r = 0.12 at y = 0.62, r = 0.40 at y = 0.38, half-step offset 'so no inner box hides behind an outer one') - a placement statement, readable at N = 4. At N = 3 only one of the two can be built, so what stands here is example_3_2's two levels with nbody's rule for WHICH body goes where: bodies 0 and 2 inner at r = 0.14, y = +0.12; body 1 outer at r = 0.34, y = -0.12; all at rest, which both members specify. That one word carries the whole argument by itself. lattice = nbody's, and the only one of its five that is deterministic: per_side = ceil(N^(1/3)) is 2 at N = 3, so the first three cells of a 2x2x2 grid are three corners of a cube, coplanar, at rest. Its own note calls it 'the least stable arrangement in the set', and the measurement agrees - it is the one configuration whose unperturbed track (0.4249) comes near the clip radius. hierarchical = three_body's, a tight binary plus a distant third at the source's own 1:4 ratio (separation 0.135, third at 0.54 from the pair centre), the inner pair on its exact circular mutual orbit as the source has it. It is a THIRD kind of word again, and worth naming as such: hierarchical is neither a shape nor a solution but a DYNAMICAL CLASS, defined by a ratio of timescales - here 6.17 inner orbits inside 0.945 of one outer orbit. figure_eight = three_body's, and it is the Chenciner-Montgomery choreography rebuilt from the published unit constants at L = SYS_R, not quoted. lagrange = three_body's, the equilateral triangle turning rigidly at omega = sqrt(3 G m / a^3) = 4.624213, v = 1.387264, period 1.358758 s - THE SAME THREE POINTS AS ring, by construction, both taken from the same radius and the same three angles. READING, three values, and it is this synthesis's OWN axis. No member declares one: all three declare `evidence` (result | trace | longhand | axiom), which asks what is drawn of a RUNNING simulation. `reading` asks something narrower that the family cannot currently answer - how much of the initial condition survives - so it is synthesis-introduced, which is a weaker warrant than a derived axis and is recorded as such. start = the three bodies at t = 0 and nothing else, the configuration as a placement; no velocity is drawn, because an arrangement does not carry one, and that is exactly why ring and lagrange are one picture here. path = the integrated trajectories as tubes. drift = the same trajectories with the perturbed run over them: body 0 moved PERTURB = 0.0005 m, half a millimetre, 0.167% of the system radius, then re-centred on the barycentre so both runs start with the same centre of mass and the same total momentum. The perturbed track is GOLD - three_body_problem's and nbody_simulation's own Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.35), the colour both use for the thing in the room that is NOT the instance - and it is 0.0120 wide against the widest coloured tube's 0.0105, so the reading is direct: gold alone means the two runs agree to within a tube width, colour beside the gold means they have parted. THE MEASURED RESULT, taken before any capture, as the largest body-to-body distance between the two runs after 1.360 s: lagrange 0.0072, figure_eight 0.0087, hierarchical 0.0305 - against ring 0.3731, shells 0.3880, lattice 0.5221, column 0.5456. A factor of fifty between the two groups, and the split is NOT arrangement-versus-solution, which is where this pass corrects its own brief: `ring` is an arrangement AND a homographic solution, and it fails, while `hierarchical` is not an exact solution at all and it holds. What separates them is whether the three ever come close: minimum pairwise separations are lagrange 0.5196, figure_eight 0.2071, ring 0.1686, hierarchical 0.1292, column 0.0467, shells 0.0004, lattice 0.0002 - and ring breaks even that ordering, because its homographic dive amplifies an error that hierarchical's steady coil does not. THE ARITHMETIC IS FIXED AND STATED: velocity-Verlet (symplectic, second order), h = 0.0005 s, 2720 steps, T = 1.360 s, G = 1, m = 1 for all three bodies, one sample every 10 steps so every track is 272 spans. The window is 1.0009 Lagrange periods, 1.308 figure-eight periods and 0.945 of hierarchical's outer orbit. Forces use a minimum-separation clamp at R_MIN = 0.05 m, which is the FAMILY'S OWN DEVICE and not a softening invented here - nbody clamps r into [0.01, 0.15], three_body refuses any pair closer than 0.1 - and it is never reached by ring, hierarchical, figure_eight or lagrange, so all four, including both exact solutions, are integrated under Newton's law unmodified. It bites only for column, shells and lattice, which are the three that collapse. WHY THE INTEGRATOR IS NOT THE MEMBERS': both members step with semi-implicit Euler (CelestialBody does velocity += force/mass*delta then position += velocity*delta; nbody does vel += acc then pos += vel with no delta at all), and under Euler at any usable step the choreography loses its shape inside one period, so the sheet would have measured integrator error and reported it as physics. EXTENTS, since seven configurations have no business being the same size and are not: start figures span 0.555 m (shells) to 0.804 m (hierarchical) across, unperturbed tracks reach 0.2774 to 0.4249 m from the centre, and three perturbed tracks would reach 0.5490 (ring), 0.5386 (lattice) and 0.7576 m (column) if they were not clipped at 0.44. The yard absorbs all of it: the AABB is 1.00 x 1.00 x 1.00 in every one of the twenty-one cells because the plate and the posts are the largest things in the scene and nothing drawn can reach them.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: ring against lagrange, in the start reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: AN IDENTITY, not an estimate, and that is what makes it worth registering. Both values call the same three angles (90, 210, 330 degrees) at the same radius (SYS_R = 0.30) through the same two lines of code; the ONLY difference between them in the file is the scalar `speed`, which multiplies the velocity array and nothing else. `start` draws bodies and no velocity. So the two frames are the same triangle of three spheres in the same yard, vertex for vertex, and the predicted focus is 0.00% with the predicted frame also 0.00%. WHY THE PHASE IS THE SAME AND WHY THAT IS FAIR: a ring of three at radius R IS the equilateral triangle at circumradius R - the only freedom either word leaves is the phase, and the phase is not part of either word, so giving them different phases would have been the rigged version, not this. VERIFIED IN THE REPLICA, rasterised BEFORE ANY CAPTURE in the critic's own currency: the geometry rebuilt in Python from the same constants and the same integrator, projected through capture_config_sweep's camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, framing 0.50 on the 1.00 m yard, which IS the union AABB), z-buffered with the default rig's ambient plus key plus fill and flat shading, then run through artifact_dna_critic's pipeline unchanged - crop to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralise each frame's own corner background, grey, resize 160 x 160, mean of the hottest 5 percent. THE CONTEXT IS THE start READING and the ranking is computed inside it. All 21 configuration pairs within start, focus percent, ascending: ring-lagrange 0.00, then 2.66, 2.66, 2.70, 2.70, 2.77, 2.83, 2.89, 2.97, 2.97, 2.99, 3.04, 3.06, 3.06, 3.12, 3.13, 3.16, 3.16, 3.21, 3.21, 3.35. The gap from the null to the runner-up (figure_eight against lagrange, 2.66) is 2.66 points, and every other pair in start sits in a band 0.69 points wide - which is the second half of the claim: at `start` the seven configurations are all about equally different from each other, EXCEPT for the one pair that is not different at all. THE SAME PAIR IN THE OTHER TWO READINGS, which is what falsifies the reading axis rather than the null: within path, ring-lagrange is 4.19 and is still the CLOSEST of the 21 (next 5.24, hottest 10.45); within drift it is 9.85 and is no longer closest (figure_eight-lagrange takes that at 8.77, hottest 14.84). So the pair that is identical at start is merely nearest at path and ordinary at drift, and the axis has done its work. FULL PREDICTED SHEET, focus percent. Configuration pairs within path: 4.19, 5.24, 6.14, 7.46, 7.64, 7.96, 7.96, 8.08, 8.24, 8.43, 8.75, 8.82, 8.94, 9.22, 9.28, 9.48, 9.70, 9.97, 9.97, 10.26, 10.45. Within drift: 8.77, 9.85, 10.54, 10.98, 11.34, 12.10, 12.51, 12.58, 12.61, 12.87, 13.07, 13.15, 13.33, 13.56, 13.58, 13.64, 13.73, 14.29, 14.30, 14.60, 14.84. Reading pairs at fixed configuration (start-path / start-drift / path-drift): ring 2.92 / 7.87 / 8.22, column 6.33 / 10.66 / 6.94, shells 4.54 / 7.49 / 6.76, lattice 5.54 / 12.21 / 10.82, hierarchical 5.68 / 10.43 / 11.11, figure_eight 1.48 / 3.39 / 3.89, lagrange 1.84 / 4.07 / 4.85. NOTE THE CONDITIONAL, and read the per-pair rows rather than the headline: the `reading` axis is predicted at 12.21 percent at its hottest (lattice, start against drift) and at 1.48 percent at its weakest (figure_eight, start against path), a factor of eight, and the weak cells are figure_eight and lagrange - the two exact solutions, whose tracks are thin closed curves that barely move under the nudge. That is not the axis failing at those cells, it IS the axis reporting the thesis, and a headline peak would hide it. Subject share of frame runs 20.82 to 23.64 percent across all twenty-one tiles, so no tile is near the blank bar. THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR everywhere except the null. The replica has one ambient term, two directional terms, flat shading, no shadows, no AO, no antialiasing and no emission falloff, and every prior prediction in this corpus under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x. The null cannot come back below 0.00, so its falsification is the other direction: anything above 0.5 percent on ring-against-lagrange at start means something outside the axis is moving between frames. If the OTHER numbers come back below these, check the harness before the design: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py, in case a value the code cannot reach fell back to the default; (b) _rejects.json, because all three exports are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=21, because at build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9 the 7 x 3 cross product is trimmed from the tail and `reading` collapses to [start] alone, which deletes both other readings and leaves the null intact but unfalsifiable. THE ONE PLACE THE REPLICA CANNOT BE TRUSTED, stated rather than discovered later: shells, lattice and column pass within 0.5 mm of each other, well inside the R_MIN clamp, and a passage that close is chaotic. The artifact integrates in PackedFloat64Array for exactly this reason, but its sqrt and its summation order are not the replica's, so the post-encounter halves of those three tracks will differ in detail between the two. Their predicted numbers are soft. The registered pair is in `start` and involves no integration at all.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION, and it is the thesis rather than a spare check. Both values enter the same branch of _initial and are written by the same two lines: position from cos/sin of the same three angles at the same SYS_R, velocity from the same expression times a scalar `speed`. The scalar is the only thing that differs - 1.0 for lagrange, RING_FRAC = 0.70 for ring - and `start` draws no velocity. A stage manager's ring of three and Lagrange's equilateral triangle ARE the same placement; the theorem is not in the placement, it is in the one number the placement does not carry. Predicted 0.00 percent focus and 0.00 percent frame; anything above 0.5 percent is render noise, and anything above 2 percent means something outside the configuration axis is moving between the two frames.

dna.designed_nulls_why: One null, and it is the whole experiment rather than a corroborating detail: if `configuration` named one kind of thing, no two of its seven values could be the same picture. The tempting second null is deliberately NOT registered and is the nearest thing to one on the reading axis - figure_eight, path against drift, where a half-millimetre nudge moves the tracks by 8.7 mm against tubes 10.5 mm wide, so the gold sleeve very nearly swallows the difference. It is predicted at 3.89 percent rather than zero, because the gold is a colour change as well as a shape change, and predicting it as a null would have been claiming an identity where there is only a small number. THE ANTI-NULL matters as much: the SAME pair that is 0.00 at start is 4.19 at path and 9.85 at drift. If ring-against-lagrange comes back at 0.00 in all three readings, the reading axis never reached the artifact and nothing else in this sheet can be believed.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand all seven configurations in a row (layout=ladder, 1.15 m pitch, about 7.9 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so a seven-wide row in the same spec would frame every single variant against nearly eight metres and photograph the yard as a chip. layout is an export and not an axis, and it ships at single, so the fixture is a belt over braces. WHAT IS NOT FIXTURED, and why nothing needs to be: there is no random knob and no clock here. There is no randf, no RandomNumberGenerator, no noise, no _process, no _physics_process and no Timer anywhere in the file - the whole figure, integration included, is built synchronously inside _ready from seven initial-condition tables and one fixed-step integrator, so the frame is complete at frame one and two builds of one value are the same mesh. That is worth saying because all three sources need fixtures and this one does not: nbody_simulation had to add a spawn_seed because four of its five configurations are RNG draws, and example_3_2 had to add BOTH a spawn_seed and a clock=hold, because its bodies wrap the tank about every third frame and an arrangement there survives roughly a thirtieth of a second. This bench integrates at BUILD time and draws the result as static geometry, which is the same move nbody's own `trace` value makes and the reason its `still_note` says the axis is legible in a single frame by construction rather than by luck.
dna.kin: three_body_problem is the nearest kin and the reason this artifact is not a duplicate of it. It owns two of the seven values outright, its `configuration` is where the word comes from, and it is already the corpus's exhibit for 'determinism and predictability are not the same thing'. What it cannot do is stand its own five values next to anybody else's: its axis is five answers in one vocabulary, and the claim here is about what happens when three vocabularies are put on one scale. It is also a live simulation with a wobble (its _physics_process writes rotation.y = sin(t*0.2)*0.4 on the whole node) where this is a still by construction. nbody_simulation is the other close kin and is the artifact that already noticed half of this: its registry says in as many words that three_body's values 'could not be taken, because figure_eight and lagrange are theorems about exactly three bodies and mean nothing at twenty', and calls that 'a real divergence, stated rather than papered over'. This bench is the object that divergence implies - it goes the other way, down to N = 3, where all three vocabularies can be spoken, and reports what the statistical words cost at that count. example_3_2_forces_with_arbitrary_angular_motion_vr contributes three of the seven words and the one honest confession in the family: its own fixture_why says that in a live placement 'its translation half is gone within about 30 ms', which is the strongest existing statement that a `configuration` axis is a claim about what an exhibit is RELEASED as and not about what it settles into. This bench is that claim held still for 1.360 s and then asked whether it mattered. ON THE MAP SIDE all three members live in the `forces` sequence and two of them also in `physicssimulation`; nbody and three_body already list each other in cluster_with, and example_3_2's seven placements (ForcesSystems, Corridor_ForcesSystems, VFM_03_Motion, Corridor_VFM_03_Motion, Trial_eye_VFM_03_Motion, Forces_6, Curation_Bay_forces_5) are the rooms where the word is currently spoken with no way to hear that it is being spoken three ways. A room holding this yard at reading=start beside three_body_problem is saying the same sentence twice; a room holding it at reading=drift beside three_body_problem is saying the sentence and then testing it. ON THE VALUE SIDE the inheritance is unusually literal for a synthesis - seven of seven `configuration` words are members', in their own spellings - and the one thing invented here is the `reading` axis, which is recorded as synthesis-introduced in the note rather than dressed up.
declines: THE BRIEF'S ARGUMENT, corrected from the code and from the measurement. The brief said only one of the three kinds survives being perturbed and that it is not the one you can draw. Half of that is wrong. `ring` - the stage arrangement, the one you can draw - turns out to be an exact solution too: three equal masses at the vertices of an equilateral triangle form a CENTRAL CONFIGURATION, so any purely tangential equal speed produces a homographic solution in which the triangle stays exactly equilateral and only its size follows a Kepler radial orbit. At RING_FRAC = 0.70 that is an ellipse of eccentricity 0.51, verified in the replica as a minimum pairwise separation of 0.1686 = 0.09735 * sqrt(3). And `hierarchical`, which is not an exact solution at all, HOLDS under the same nudge (0.0305) where ring does not (0.3731). So the split is not arrangement-versus-theorem. Measured, it is whether the three bodies ever come close, with ring as the exception that proves it needed measuring: it never comes closer than 0.169 and still fails, because its homographic dive amplifies at periapsis what hierarchical's steady coil never amplifies at all. The brief's sentence is kept as the QUESTION and its answer is replaced by the number.

three_body_problem's `pinwheel`, its own default and the value every one of its five placements currently renders. It is declined on the code's authority: the .tscn authors Body1 (-5,0,0) with velocity (0,0,3) and Body2 (5,0,0) with (0,0,-3), which is a consistent circulation, and then Body3 (0,0,5) with (-3,0,0) - which is the OPPOSITE sense; a pinwheel wants (+3,0,0) there. Two bodies go one way and the third the other, the total momentum is (-3,0,0) rather than zero, and the barycentre drifts out of the frame. Its own registry already records the consequence without naming the cause: 'pinwheel and near_collision drift and draw the line' at evidence=axiom. Importing it would have put a figure in this yard whose centre of mass leaves through the wall, in a bench whose every other value is barycentre-centred so that one camera can photograph seven figures fairly. It is the first thing to add if the axis ever needs an eighth, and it should be added under its own name - `pinwheel` is a good word for two-against-one, which is what the numbers say it is.

three_body_problem's `near_collision`. It is nearly collinear and barely moving, so it falls together, slingshots, and usually ejects one body - which at this yard's scale means a track that leaves through the wall in the first third of the window and is drawn as a stub. `column` and `lattice` already carry the collapse case with far more of the picture inside the yard, and a fourth value whose whole content is 'it left' would have been a tile that argues by absence. Declined for framing, and the framing is measured: the perturbed `column` track already reaches 0.7576 m against a 0.50 m plate and has to be clipped.

nbody_simulation's `cloud` and example_3_2's `scatter` - the null pole BOTH members declare, and the most tempting value in the set. Declined because at N = 3 it is not a distribution, it is one arbitrary arrangement, and with a pinned seed a still cannot tell it from an authored one; the word only means something at N large. That is not a limitation of this bench, it is the statistical vocabulary's own first casualty at the count where the exact-solution vocabulary is defined at all, and it belongs in the argument rather than in the sheet. Declining it also removed the last RNG from the file, so this artifact needs no seed fixture where both of its generative sources needed one.

nbody_simulation's `disc` and `binary`, and they are declined for two different reasons worth separating. `disc` is an annulus in XZ with tangential velocities - at N = 3, with three samples, an annulus is indistinguishable from a circle, so it would have been a second `ring` with jitter, and its jitter is an RNG draw besides. `binary` is more interesting: its code splits at i >= n/2, and 3/2 is 1 in integer division, so at N = 3 nbody's `binary` is one body on the left and two on the right - EXACTLY three_body's `hierarchical` split, arrived at by an integer division rather than by a claim. It could not be built as its own value because without the random clump jitter its two right-hand bodies land on the same point. So the two words collapse into one placement at N = 3 and the honest thing is one value, `hierarchical`, with the collapse recorded here.

nbody_simulation's `shells` as a separate value from example_3_2's. This was the strongest candidate for an eighth value and it is declined because a spherical shell of three points is not a shell - it is a triangle at an angle - so the value would have been a fact about how three random points on two spheres happened to land, pinned by a seed, and would have looked like a worse `lattice`. What the disagreement deserved was a sentence, not a tile, and it has one in the note.

The members' `evidence` axis (result | trace | longhand | axiom), which all three of them declare, character for character, along with example_2_8, example_2_9, koch_curve, wave_interference_tank and eighteen others. It is the family's most widely shared vocabulary and it is a DIFFERENT question: evidence asks what is drawn of a running simulation, and every one of its four values presupposes that the simulation is the subject. `reading` asks how much of the initial condition survives, which is a question about the axis this bench is actually turning. A yard that swept both would be answering two questions in one sheet and could not attribute either. It is also the axis that would have made this a duplicate: three_body_problem at configuration=lagrange, evidence=trace already exists and is a placement anyone can walk to.

Mass. All three bodies are equal here and that is not laziness, it is a precondition: the Chenciner-Montgomery choreography exists only for equal masses, and the Lagrange triangle's stability depends on the mass ratio through Gascheau's condition - 27(m1m2 + m2m3 + m3m1) < (m1+m2+m3)^2, which for equal masses reads 81 < 9 and fails, so the equal-mass Lagrange triangle is linearly UNSTABLE. That is a fact this sheet is quietly reporting and could not report if the masses were a knob: lagrange holds at 0.0072 over one period not because it is stable but because its e-folding time is longer than the window, and a longer window would show it come apart. A mass axis is the honest sequel and it would need a different, longer integration.

Animation, a clock, a scrub, and any live simulation at all. Two of the three sources are live and both had to fixture their way to a photograph - example_3_2 needed clock=hold because its arrangement survives about a thirtieth of a second, three_body_problem needed nothing but wobbles its own node every frame. A still cannot tell 0.3 s of a run from 0.9 s of it, and `reading` would be trivially confusable with how far a single run had got. Nothing in this file has a clock; the integration happens at build time and the result is geometry.

Grabbing, and letting a hand place the bodies. That is the artifact three_body_problem's own @identity asks for by name ('Missing: VR grabbable bodies to set initial conditions by hand') and it is a good one. It is not this one: a hand-placed initial condition cannot be photographed against six others, and this bench exists to put seven vocabularies in one sheet where they can be compared.

The yard's dimensions, the body radius, the tube radii, the clip radius, the perturbation, the integrator step, the window and every colour. None of these are exports. The yard is pinned because it IS the fixed AABB; the tube radii are pinned and NESTED because in a choreography all three bodies run one curve and three equal tubes would be a depth-fight rather than a picture; the step and the window are pinned so that seven configurations are given the same amount of computation and can be compared on it.

A larger figure inside the yard. Every configuration could be scaled up and every pair would read hotter, but the yard's margin is what keeps the drift tracks inside their bounds - a perturbed column already runs to 0.7576 m and has to be clipped at 0.44, and clipping more of the sheet to gain contrast would be buying a number with the evidence.
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=21. `configuration` is declared first and is never trimmed; `reading` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap, so at the default --max=9 the 7 x 3 sheet renders as 7 x 1 = start only. That cap would leave the registered null intact and make it unfalsifiable, because with one reading value there is no reading axis left for the same pair to stop being null in - and the anti-null (ring against lagrange at 0.00 / 4.19 / 9.85 across the three readings) is the only thing that distinguishes a working sheet from one where the reading axis never reached the artifact. READ THE PER-PAIR ROWS, not the headline: `reading` is predicted to peak at 12.21 percent (lattice, start against drift) and to bottom at 1.48 percent (figure_eight, start against path), and the weak cells are the two exact solutions, which is the thesis rather than a weakness.
